subject: Renewal/Expansion: mid-year capacity bump and billing alignment
messages:

Date: 2026-08-12 09:15 PDT
Subject: Capacity bump & invoice alignment question

Hi Soojin,

Quick question from our side as we approach renewal: our usage for Q3 is trending ~40% above current committed capacity due to a new feature rollout. We have a renewal in November and would prefer to avoid another line item invoice mid-cycle if possible. Options we were hoping you could confirm:

- Add capacity mid-contract and have charges flow into the Nov renewal invoice (annualize), OR
- Top-up now with a one-time charge + a credit against Nov invoice, OR
- Any blended/phase approach Redwood has used before (discounting on top-up vs voucher)

Also if there's any standard discount bands for mid-contract growth, please share. We may need a PO amendment from procurement (cc'd).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if that helps.

Emma Shaw
Head of Platform
BrightOps

Hi Emma — thanks for the heads up and the usage CSV.

We're happy to support the mid-cycle bump. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Marissa (finance) to weigh in on the preferred billing pattern and any discount we can extend for a mid-contract add. Quick answers up front:

- We can either top-up now (charged immediately) with a credit applied at renewal, or we can amend the commitment to annualize the additional capacity so it flows into the Nov invoice.
- For a ~40% uplift we typically recommend a blended approach: a small immediate charge for the incremental tokens to cover near-term spend + an annualized commit increase at a modest banded discount.

Ben/Marissa — can you confirm numbers (target: 40% uplift, effective 8/1) and pricing approach? If finance needs a one-line amendment + DocuSign, Marissa can advise.

I'll prep a short one-pager to share with Emma once we have the internal alignment.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

Thanks for the tag. Cutting to the recommendation so Soojin can share with the customer:

Proposed commercial path (BrightOps — 40% uplift, effective 8/1):
1) Immediate top-up: charge for incremental usage from 8/1–10/31 (pro-rated) at list rates, with a temporary 10% one-time uplift discount applied to the incremental portion.
2) Renewal amendment: increase committed capacity starting 11/1 to reflect the new baseline (40% higher). For the committed uplift we can offer a 12% blended discount on the uplifted capacity for the remaining term (annualized).
3) Billing alignment: finance issues the one-time invoice for the pro-rated period; we'll post a credit memo equal to 100% of the one-time discount then apply it against the Nov renewal invoice to avoid double-billing concerns.

Rationale: keeps cashflow neutral for Redwood while offering BrightOps a meaningful blended saving and clean co-term at renewal.

I attached a quick model with numbers at 3 different uplift sizes — see sheet 'BrightOps_sample' for the 40% case.

Attachments: pricing_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Emma — thanks for the patience. Below is the proposal based on our internal review. Summarizing the plan and next steps so procurement has everything they need.

Summary proposal (BrightOps request: ~40% uplift effective 8/1):
- Immediate pro-rated charge (8/1–10/31) on incremental capacity at list, with a 10% one-time discount on that incremental portion. Invoice to be issued upon PO or acceptance.
- Commitment amendment to annualize the uplift starting 11/1 with a 12% blended discount on the uplifted commit for the term.
- We will issue a credit memo equal to the one-time discount and apply it against the Nov renewal invoice.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: send PO for the one-time pro-rated amount OR confirm you prefer DocuSign amendment.
2) If DocuSign: Marissa will send the amendment link (DocuSign) and an attached one-pager that explains the arithmetic.
3) If PO: please include billing entity and PO number so we can get finance to queue the invoice.

If that looks good I'd propose a short 20-min call tomorrow to run the numbers live — happy to share the model.

Thanks,
